claims.text: WTaTiVZr consists of reduced-activation refractory elements.
The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar.
The WTaTiVZr alloy is chemically homogeneous.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has a single-phase BCC or BCC-like structure.
Atomic-size and modulus mismatches produce severe lattice distortion in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion shifts WTaTiVZr plasticity from screw-dislocation-dominated to edge-dislocation-dominated deformation.
Plastic deformation in pure tungsten is dominated by screw dislocations under the stated high-temperature conditions.
Edge dislocations in WTaTiVZr have enhanced mobility relative to screw dislocations.
Lattice distortion lowers the effective barriers for edge-dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced edge-dislocation activity produces more homogeneous plastic flow and greater plastic-strain accommodation.
More uniform edge-dislocation activity delays crack initiation.
Screw dislocations in pure tungsten are comparatively less mobile at high temperature and cause early crack nucleation.
WTaTiVZr will have greater plastic strain and ductility than pure tungsten under identical loading at 673–1073 K.
WTaTiVZr will have greater toughness than pure tungsten under identical loading at 673–1073 K.
TEM will reveal a high density of mobile edge dislocations and associated networks in deformed WTaTiVZr.
TEM will reveal predominantly screw dislocations in deformed pure tungsten.
Prior evidence establishes dislocation-mediated creep in TaTiVWZr.
Prior evidence supports specifically edge-dislocation-dominated plasticity in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The range 673–1073 K is relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Matching grain size, surface finish, atmosphere, temperature, and strain rate provides a controlled WTaTiVZr-versus-tungsten comparison.

contradictions.description: The initial state asserts a chemically homogeneous, single-phase alloy and the boundary excludes extraneous phases, while the uncertainty field concedes that incidental nanoprecipitates or second phases in this specific alloy may influence toughness. The actual phase state is therefore treated as both established and unresolved.
